title: SSE flush negotiation and tool-call safety for resumable streams
creator: Aisha Chen
description:
Problem: Our current SSE resume story is brittle when streams interleave structured function/tool-call frames with plain token deltas. Clients either drop partial function outputs or re-execute tool-calls after reconnect, causing duplication and unexpected side-effects. Additionally, clients have no reliable way to know which flushed tokens are durable server-side vs still buffered in aggregator layers (leading to duplicate requests and poor UX).

Goal: Define and implement a minimal negotiation and framing extension on top of SSE that: (1) provides explicit flush semantics so clients can safely assume durability boundaries, (2) makes function/tool-call frames idempotent or safely resumable across reconnects, (3) supports graceful fallback for legacy clients (HTTP long-poll / chunked) and (4) exposes observability hooks (flush events, resume tokens, per-chunk provenance ids).

Proposal summary: 1) Add a lightweight handshake exchange at subscription start: client sends a `streamCapabilities` JSON hint indicating expected tool-call behavior (idempotent, exactly-once preferred, allow-replay) and maximum resume window. Server responds with `streamState` indicating resumeToken format (opaque vs sequence), heartbeat interval, and whether the server will attach per-chunk provenance headers. 2) Chunk framing: every SSE data chunk includes fields: `chunk_id` (uuid), `seq` (monotonic per-connection), `type` (delta | function_call | flush | heartbeat), and optional `checksum` for payload integrity. 3) Flush semantics: servers emit explicit `flush` frames that mark a durability boundary. Clients should treat content up to the latest `flush` chunk_id as durable. 4) Function-call safe resume: function-call frames include `call_id` (deterministic by prompt+meta) and an optional `replay_hint` that tells clients whether the call has side-effects and if it is safe to retry. Server will persist minimal call manifest (call_id -> result reference) for the configured resume window to allow replay without double-execution when possible. 5) Reconnect behavior: on reconnect clients present the last observed `chunk_id` and optional `last_flush_id`. Server validates and either issues a delta replay from the next seq or sends a `rebase` frame containing a compact manifest for reconstructing call results. 6) Backpressure & pacing: server may send `backpressure_hints` in meta events indicating recommended client read window; clients should reduce inflight request concurrency accordingly.

Trade-offs and rationale: - Persisting call manifests for exact-once semantics increases memory/storage; we bound this by the negotiated resume window and evict policies. - Deterministic call_id generation is not foolproof for high-entropy inputs; we will prefer server-side manifest where available. - Checksum and chunk metadata increase wire overhead; we keep fields minimal and optional for legacy/low-bandwidth clients.

Compatibility: - Legacy clients: if a client doesn't send `streamCapabilities`, server behaves in best-effort mode (no resume guarantees, periodic heartbeat only). - HTTP fallback: provide same framing encoded as JSONL over chunked transfer; will document differences and provide compatibility shims in the SDKs.

Observability & debugging: expose chunk-level metrics (latency-to-flush, gap-frequency), and integrate `chunk_id`/`call_id` into logs and tracing so Ops can correlate reconnect gaps to customer-visible errors.

Implementation plan: Phase 1 (PoC) implement handshake, metadata framing, and flush frames in the hosted runtime (internal flag). Phase 2 implement server-side call manifest for replay within resume window and SDK client support for resume handshake. Phase 3: bake evictions, metrics, console integration, and upgrades to Dedicated nodes.

Success criteria: - Client SDKs can reconnect from within the resume window without duplicate function execution in >=90% of test scenarios. - <1% of customer streams observe data duplication after reconnect during canary. - Observability surfaces show chunk_id correlation in traces and consoles.
comments: 2026-03-10 Aisha Chen: Created ticket after postmortem showed duplicated tool calls in customer workspace when network flapped. Initial design doc linked.
2026-03-11 Marco Rivera: Implemented PoC framing in local runtime branch. Basic handshake works; need to decide on deterministic call_id scheme and storage backend for call manifests.

2026-03-11 Priya Nair: Reviewed PoC; suggested adding optional checksum and explicit 'rebase' frame to provide compact state after long reconnects. Also requested telemetry events for failed resume attempts.

2026-03-12 Marco Rivera: Added checksum and rebase prototype. Found edge case where HTTP/2 multiplexers reorder small frames — we now include seq numbers to detect reordering. Next: update JS/Go SDKs to send streamCapabilities and surface last_flush_id to server on reconnect.
2026-03-12 SRE note: Dashboard panel created for stream chunk latency; will watch during canary. Added alert if resume success rate < 95% for a deployment window.
